question.leadin: The final holder of this title was Tokugawa Yoshinobu.
question.text: Prior to an 1868 restoration of imperial rule, what title was held by military rulers of Japan?
question.clue: Two successive dynasties in this position supported the illegitimate Northern Court.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about emperors of Japan.
swap.text: This man has the distinction of maintaining the longest reign of any Japanese emperor. He is more famously known for overseeing the Japanese surrender during World War II.
swap.clue: This ruler, who delivered the Jewel Voice Broadcast, later renounced his divinity in the Humanity Declaration.

question.text: Prior to the Perry Expedition, the only Japanese port that was largely open to foreigners was this city on the southern island of Kyushu. It later became the second city to be hit with an atomic bomb during World War II.
question.clue: Trade between this city and Macau was carried out by non-American "black ships."

swap.leadin: Its founder was one of the three great unifiers of a certain country, along with Oda Nobunaga and Toyotomi Hideyoshi.
swap.text: Name this shogunate, which was established after the Battle of Sekigahara and ruled from 1603 to 1868.
swap.clue: People who passed this period's fumi-e tests often remained "hidden" afterwards.

question.leadin: This battle saw the use of Portuguese arquebuses, and one side of this battle consisted of forces loyal to Toyotomi Hideyori.
question.text: Name this battle that saw the forces of Ishida Mitsunari and Mori Terumoto defeated by those of Tokugawa Ieyasu, thereby establishing his namesake shogunate.
question.clue: The capture of Konosu and Gifu Castles preceded this battle, whose decisive moment saw a staged round of arquebus fire signal a force of turncoats to attack the army of their initial ally Otani instead.

swap.text: This document officially ceded power to Emperor Meiji whose third clause allowed the ability to pursue any occupation regardless of social standing.
swap.clue: This declaration was issued by the Meiji Emperor after he took the throne. "Evil customs of the past" were done away with after this document was issued, as it paved the way for the westernization of Japan.

question.leadin: Answer the following about Japanese history prior to the Meiji Restoration.
question.text: This city was the capital of Japan until Emperor Meiji made Tokyo the capital in 1868.
question.clue: Henry Stimson, the US Secretary of War, is said to have honeymooned here, and famously lobbied to have this city taken off the list of bombing targets during the Second World War despite significant protests from the military.

swap.leadin: Manchuria was given back to China through the terms of this treaty.
swap.text: Identify this agreement which saw one side gain control of half of Sakhalin Island.
swap.clue: For brokering this treaty, which the parties signed in Kittery, Maine, U.S. president Theodore Roosevelt received the Nobel Peace Prize.

question.text: This first Shogunate began after Minamoto Yoritomo defeated the Tairas at the Battle of Dannoura in 1185. It was late dominated by the Hojo family.
question.clue: Before a major battle one leader of this polity meditated to find the source of cowardice in himself, and one conflict during it occurred when the cloistered emperor Go-Toba attempted to take the throne.

swap.leadin: Moderator note: do not reveal the alternate answer to the first bonus part. The man who negotiated this treaty gave the emperor an ultimatum from President Fillmore and then left the country for a year.
swap.text: Identify this 1854 treaty which opened up the ports of Shimoda and Hakodate in Japan to American trade.
swap.clue: Signed aboard the USS Powhatan, one provision of it mandated hospitality to shipwrecked sailors and their free travel within certain limits.

question.text: Admirals Togo and Rozhestvensky faced off in this pivotal naval victory for Japan in the Russo-Japanese War, which was fought in the narrows between the Korean peninsula and Honshu.
question.answerHtml: Battle of Tsushima Strait/s [or Tsusimskoye srazheniye; prompt on Battle of the Sea of Japan]
question.clue: At the end of this battle, Admiral Nebogatov surrendered rather than doom his 2,000-plus sailors; regardless, his fleet had lost six battleships and twenty-eight other ships in a single day after eight months of sailing from the Baltic Sea.

swap.text: The Meiji emperor put down this 1877 rebellion, led by Saigo Takamori, who lamented the loss of power of his fellow Samurais. It fought its last battle at Shiroyama.
swap.clue: Many leaders of this movement were on the losing side of the Seikanron Debate, in which they had unsuccessfully advocated a war, and thereafter they had resigned and returned to their home prefecture.

question.leadin: Answer some questions about famous war photographers.
question.text: Joe Rosenthal took an iconic image of five marines raising a flag on this Pacific Island during World War II. Clint Eastwood directed a film told from the Japanese perspective called Letters from This place.
question.clue: The February to March 1945 struggle for this island at Meatgrinder Hill and Mount Suribachi ended with a certain flag-raising.

swap.text: This research group under the Kwantung Army committed some of the greatest Japanese crimes against humanity during the war. It was commanded by Shiro Ishii, who was pardoned by the United States after the war in exchange for his data.
swap.answerHtml: Unit 731 [accept Nana-san-ichi Butai; accept Epidemic Prevention and Water Purification Department of the Kwantung Army; accept Kantogun Boeki Kyusuibu Honbu]
swap.clue: This group within the Epidemic Prevention and Purification Department. A guy actually named Colonel Sanders brought it to the attention of Douglas MacArthur, who pardoned its leader in exchange for scientific data.

question.text: This period, in which Suiko ("soo-ee-ko") and Shotoku ruled, saw several notable Korean monks such as Illa and Hyepyeon ("h'YEH-pyun") establish themselves in Japan. This period lies between the Kofun and Nara periods.
question.clue: Prince Shotoku proclaimed the Confucian 17 Article Constitution during this period, part of a series of moves to adopt Chinese customs.

swap.text: Perry negotiated this treaty, which mandated reasonable treatment of shipwrecked sailors and opened the ports of Hakodate and Shimoda.

question.leadin: Identify these leaders of 20th century Japan.
question.text: This man served as Emperor of Japan from 1912 to 1926. His reign is considered a golden age of Japanese democracy.
question.clue: This ruler, who ceded regency power to his son due to psychological problems. His country sent a list of twenty-one demands to a neighbor.

swap.leadin: Unlike the Gishi Wajinden, this chronicle makes little mention of Empress Himiko, a semi-mythical shaman queen who established relations with Cao Wei ("tsao way").
swap.text: Name this work, which was completed eight years after the Kojiki and chronicles national myths and history up to the 8th century.
swap.clue: This set of chronicles, the most comprehensive text available for scholarship on Ancient Japan. It was completed under the supervision of Prince Toneri and presented to Empress Gensho in the year 720.

question.text: The Tokugawa shogun Iemitsu instituted this system, which required each of the daimyo to spend a part of the year in Edo and leave family members as hostages in order to prevent rebellion.

swap.text: In the 1651 Keian Uprising, Yui Shosetsu gathered an army of these master-less mercenary samurai and attempted to overthrow the Tokugawa Shogunate.
swap.clue: In modern Japan, salarymen are often referred to as these people if they are unemployed.
